release.title: Canadian Survey on Business Conditions: Use of artificial intelligence by businesses, second quarter of 2026
release.highlights: In the second quarter of 2026, 19.2% of Canadian businesses used artificial intelligence (AI) in producing goods or delivering services, up from 12.2% in the second quarter of 2025. Over one in seven businesses (14.5%) planned to adopt AI over the next 12 months. Businesses in information and cultural industries (38.6%) and finance and insurance (31.5%) were most likely to use or plan to use AI, while adoption was lowest in mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction (3.4%) and agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting (4.9%). By province, AI use was highest in Ontario (16.8%) and Quebec (15.2%), compared with 8.4% in the Atlantic provinces.

methodology_rules.title: Enterprise-size confounding in regional business AI adoption comparisons
methodology_rules.rule: Do not publish raw cross-provincial or regional AI adoption rate gaps across 'All enterprise sizes' as geographic business technology differentials. Comparing Ontario (16.8%) and Atlantic Canada (8.4%) across all enterprise sizes yields an 8.4 percentage point gap, whereas holding enterprise size to large businesses (100 employees or more) yields a 2.3 percentage point gap (39.1% vs 36.8%). Over 70% of the raw regional gap reflects enterprise size distribution (concentration of large corporate headquarters vs micro-enterprises) rather than regional technological adoption propensity.

semantic_rule.explanation: Over two-thirds of the raw regional AI adoption gap reflects enterprise size composition (prevalence of micro-enterprises) rather than regional technological uptake.

methodology_rules.title: Distinguishing active AI utilization from planned future adoption
methodology_rules.rule: When reporting AI adoption metrics, prose must explicitly distinguish between current active use in production or service delivery ('used AI in the past 12 months') and forward-looking plans ('plans to use AI over the next 12 months'). Confusing active deployment with speculative adoption intentions distorts market penetration estimates.

methodology_rules.title: Multi-period adoption growth and percentage point definitions
methodology_rules.rule: Year-over-year changes in adoption percentages represent percentage point differences between two survey cross-sections (e.g. 19.2% vs 12.2% is a 7.0 percentage point increase), not relative compounding rates or individual firm transition dynamics. Prose must state percentage point changes and avoid colloquial compounding claims.

methodology_rules.title: Two-tier coverage subtraction against The Daily and Analytical Paper
methodology_rules.rule: A candidate bundle that merely restates national headline adoption figures or lead highlights already narrated in The Daily highlights should be skipped with rejection_category='already_in_daily'. A bundle that restates broad summary tables already reported in the StatCan Analytical Study (Catalogue 11-621-M) should be skipped with rejection_category='already_in_analytical_paper'.

candidate_briefs.title: Deconstructing the regional AI gap: enterprise firm size explains over 70% of the Ontario-Atlantic margin
candidate_briefs.summary: Demonstrates the descriptive drill-down nuance: while headline figures show an 8.4 percentage point gap in AI adoption between Ontario and Atlantic Canada across all enterprise sizes, large enterprises (100+ employees) adopt AI at nearly four times the rate of micro-enterprises (38.4% vs 10.4%). Restricting the comparison to large enterprises narrows the provincial gap to 2.3 percentage points, debunking the premise of an acute regional technology divide.

facts.human: across all enterprise sizes, Ontario's AI adoption rate was 16.8% compared with 8.4% in the Atlantic provinces (an 8.4 percentage point margin)
enterprises with 100 or more employees adopted AI at 38.4%, compared with 10.4% for small businesses with 1 to 19 employees
among enterprises with 100 or more employees, the gap between Ontario (39.1%) and the Atlantic provinces (36.8%) narrowed to 2.3 percentage points

candidate_briefs.title: Micro-enterprise AI adoption lag driven by information uncertainty rather than outright rejection
candidate_briefs.summary: Investigates whether small-firm AI adoption lag stems from active rejection or informational uncertainty. While active non-adoption is virtually identical between micro-enterprises and large firms (67.1% vs 65.8%), micro-enterprises report an 'Unknown' adoption status at twice the rate of large enterprises (31.4% vs 15.8%).

facts.human: businesses with 1 to 4 employees reported an unknown or uncertain status regarding future AI adoption at 31.4%, compared with 15.8% for large enterprises with 100 or more employees
rates of active non-adoption remained comparable across scale, with 67.1% of micro-enterprises and 65.8% of large enterprises stating they do not plan to adopt AI
